open: We are {place_in}!
{name} and {fr} run {place_to}.
Today is {event}, and {crowd} are already waving flags. {name}, are you ready?
Hooray, football!
The grass sparkles, and {npc} calls everyone to warm up.
The grass sparkles with dew, and {npc} is already calling the whole team to warm up. The game is soon!
The whistle!
A whistle rings over the pitch: the game will start soon!
A whistle rings over the pitch, and {fr} hops with joy. {name}, the ball is waiting!
fact: The ball has patches.
An old ball has 32 patches: 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons.
Did you know? A classic football is stitched from 32 panels: 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons.
Players keep running!
In one match a footballer runs about ten kilometres.
Did you know? In one match a footballer runs about ten kilometres. That is like a run to the next village!
Traffic light cards!
The yellow and red cards came from a traffic light.
Did you know? A referee came up with yellow and red cards after seeing a traffic light: yellow means careful, red means stop.
Stripy grass!
The stripes on a pitch are grass cut in different directions.
Did you know? The stripes on a pitch are not painted: the grass is cut in different directions, so it shines differently in the light.
fun: The ball ran away!
The ball rolled off by itself into an ice-cream cart.
The ball suddenly rolled off by itself and plopped into an ice-cream cart. Now it is as sweet as a cake!
Oh, a sock!
Someone put a sock on the ball, and now it will not bounce.
The ball sits in a warm scarf and will not bounce. {fr} laughs: "It caught a cold before the game!"
The whistle sings!
A bug flew into the whistle, and it sang like a nightingale.
A bug flew into the whistle, and instead of "fweet!" it sang like a nightingale. {crowd} clap and ask for more!
Pshhh!
The ball said "pshh" and went soft as a pancake.
The ball said "pshh" and went soft as a pancake. {fr} laughs: "Now it is a pancake match!"
final: Goal! Hooray! Champions!
{crowd} shout "hooray!", and {name} waves to everyone.
{crowd} shout "hooray!", {npc} tosses up a cap, and {name} and {fr} hug. The best day ever!
Victory, friends!
{rival} shakes hands, and now we are all one team.
{rival} smiles and shakes hands. Now the pitch has one big team, and everyone is having fun!

r: Roar of the crowd, ready, run!

open: We are {place_in}!
{name} and {fr} hurry {place_to} to warm up.
Today is {event}: running, jumping and swimming! {npc} waves little wings, and {crowd} are already clapping.
Sport, hooray!
{npc} buzzes: "Everyone to the start, friends!"
A bell rings, and {npc} buzzes: "To the start!" {name}, are you ready to run?
To the start!
The arena smells of rubber, and flags flutter in the wind.
The arena smells of new rubber, and flags flutter in the wind. {fr} is already doing squats!
fact: Medals have silver!
A gold Olympic medal is almost all silver.
Did you know? A gold Olympic medal is mostly silver, with a thin layer of gold on top.
Long ago, in Greece!
The first Olympic Games were in Greece over two thousand years ago.
Did you know? The first Olympic Games were held in Greece more than two thousand years ago, and they were repeated every four years.
The marathon is long!
Marathon runners run 42 kilometres and nearly 200 metres.
Did you know? Marathon runners run forty-two kilometres and almost two hundred metres more. That is a whole road between towns!
A spin on ice!
A skater spins faster than three turns a second.
Did you know? In a spin, a figure skater makes more than three turns a second and still stays on their feet!
fun: Laces!
The laces tied in a knot, and {fr} hops on the spot.
The laces on the trainers tied themselves in a bow, and {fr} hops on the spot like a grasshopper.
Splash! Into the pool!
A rubber duck jumped into the pool and swam front crawl.
A rubber duck jumped into the pool and swam faster than anyone. {crowd} roar with laughter and clap.
Wrong way!
{rival} runs backwards along the track, waving to everyone.
{rival} runs backwards along the track and is about to finish, but at the start. {crowd} laugh.
Bzzzz!
{npc} buzzes so loudly that the stopwatch jumps.
{npc} buzzes with joy so loudly that the stopwatch jumps and starts counting to ten by itself.
final: We are the winners!
{crowd} clap, and {name} jumps for joy.
{crowd} clap, {npc} circles overhead, and {name} and {fr} stand on the podium with their medals. We won!
The finish! Hooray!
{rival} laughs and gives everyone a little ball.
{rival} laughs and is the first to clap for the friends. Now everyone holds a medal and a kind smile!

l: Lap by lap, light and lively!

open: We are {place_in}!
{name} and {fr} hurry {place_to}.
Today is {event}! {npc} shines like a star, and {crowd} are already looking at the sky.
Three, two, one!
It is quiet {place_in}, and {npc} hums softly.
It is still quiet {place_in}, and only {npc} hums softly and whispers: "We fly soon!"
The stars wait!
Morning {place_in}: {npc} gleams and calls everyone.
Morning {place_in}: {npc} gleams in the sun and calls everyone. {name}, are you ready to fly to the stars?
fact: Footprints stay!
There is no wind on the Moon, so footprints last a very long time.
Did you know? There is no wind or rain on the Moon, so astronauts' footprints hardly fade and last a very long time.
Taller in space!
In space a person grows a few centimetres taller.
Did you know? In space, where there is no weight, the spine stretches and a person grows a few centimetres taller.
A day beats a year!
On Venus a day is longer than a year. What a strange day!
Did you know? On Venus, one spin on its axis takes longer than a whole year going round the Sun!
A blue sunset!
On Mars the sunset is blue, and the daytime sky is pinkish.
Did you know? On Mars the daytime sky looks pinkish, but the sunset around the Sun is blue. You can see it in photos.
fun: Atishoo!
{rival} sneezes, and all the moon dust swirls in the air.
{rival} breathes in dust and sneezes so loudly that the echo bounces off every crater.
Floating drops!
In zero gravity, tea does not pour. It floats in a ball.
In zero gravity tea does not pour but floats in little balls. {fr} gobbles them up, laughing.
Where is my slipper?
The slipper floated off and circles near the ceiling.
The slipper floated off and now circles the cabin like a tiny satellite. {fr} chases it!
Helmet back to front!
{rival} puts the helmet on back to front and sees only heels.
{rival} puts the helmet on back to front and sees only heels. "Lovely stars!" says {rival}.
final: Three, two, one, hooray!
The rocket takes off, and {name} waves to the stars.
Three, two, one! {npc} lifts off, {crowd} clap, and {name} and {fr} wave to the stars from the window.
Space is ours, friends!
{rival} gives everyone a little star, and we fly together.
{rival} gives everyone a little star, and now the friends are a new space crew. Off we go!

sz: Sixty stars shine as skies zoom!

open: We are in the park!
{name} and {fr} go {place_to}.
Today is {event}! {npc} polishes his glasses, and {crowd} hide behind the ferns.
Stomp, stomp, stomp!
The ground shakes: {rival} is coming to the parade!
The ground trembles: {rival} walks to the clearing where {event} will soon begin. {name}, do not be afraid, he is a friend!
Hooray, dinosaurs!
It is quiet among the ferns, and {npc} lays out his maps.
Morning {place_in}: it smells of moss, and {npc} lays out his maps and whispers: "Today we will discover something!"
fact: Hens are dino cousins!
Birds, even ordinary hens, come from dinosaurs.
Did you know? Birds came from dinosaurs, so an ordinary hen is a distant cousin of Tyrannosaurus.
Feathered dinosaurs!
Many dinosaurs had feathers, like birds.
Did you know? Scientists find feather prints on many dinosaurs. Some were as fluffy as chicks.
A banana-long tooth!
A Tyrannosaurus tooth with its root could be longer than a banana.
Did you know? A Tyrannosaurus tooth with its root could reach thirty centimetres, longer than a banana.
A thousand teeth!
Duck-billed dinosaurs had more than a thousand teeth.
Did you know? Some duck-billed dinosaurs had more than a thousand tiny teeth in their mouths, for chewing leaves.
fun: Little arms!
Tyrannosaurus arms are so short they cannot reach its nose.
{rival} cannot scratch his nose: Tyrannosaurus arms are very short. {fr} scratches it with a twig.
The snail hurries!
{npc} crawls to the parade. He set off yesterday.
{npc} crawls to the parade very proudly: he set off yesterday morning. "I am on time!" he says.
A feather-duster tail!
{rival} wags his tail, and all the leaves fly off the tree.
{rival} wags his tail with joy, and all the leaves fly off the tree. It is an autumn waltz in the middle of summer!
Plop!
Something plopped in the swamp, and {fr} jumps with fright.
Something plopped in the swamp, and {fr} jumps: "Is it an egg?" No, it is just a round pebble, and everyone laughs.
final: Hooray, little dinos!
{crowd} clap their paws, and {rival} stomps.
{crowd} clap their paws, {rival} sways everyone with his nose, and {npc} writes in his notebook: "Best day!"
All are friends!
Everyone dances at the parade, and even {rival} twirls.
Everyone dances at the parade, and even {rival} twirls so hard that the ground rocks. It is the merriest parade in the world!

open: We are {place_in}!
{name} and {fr} hurry {place_to}.
Today is {event}! {npc} snorts with a little engine, and {crowd} are already waving flags.
Brrr! Start!
Engines hum, and {npc} winks with headlights.
Engines hum across the whole track, and {npc} winks with headlights. {name}, are you ready for speed?
Hooray, racing!
Morning {place_in}: it smells of rubber and hot tea.
Morning {place_in}: it smells of tyres, the stands are noisy, and {npc} is already at the start. {fr} holds a flag.
fact: Tyres in two seconds!
In Formula 1, the four wheels change in under three seconds.
Did you know? At a pit stop, mechanics change all four wheels of a racing car in under three seconds.
Smooth tyres!
Tyres for a dry track are smooth, with no pattern.
Did you know? On a dry track racing tyres are smooth, with no pattern, to grip the road better.
The first car crawled!
The first car drove as fast as a quick bicycle.
Did you know? The first petrol car, built by Karl Benz, went about as fast as a quick cyclist.
The chequered flag!
A black and white chequered flag means the race is over.
Did you know? When a driver sees the black and white chequered flag, they know it is the finish and the race is over.
fun: Beep-beep!
The horn suddenly sang a song by itself.
The horn suddenly sang a birthday song by itself. {crowd} clap, though it is not their party.
Wipers!
The wipers wave at {crowd}, as if dancing.
The wipers on the window wave at {crowd}, as if dancing. {fr} waves back.
A wheel rolls!
A wheel wanted to play and rolled away down the path.
A wheel wanted to play and rolled away down the path. "Stop!" shouts {rival}, puffing behind it.
Soap bubbles!
At the car wash, {npc} blows soap bubbles from the pipe.
At the car wash {npc} is covered in soap foam and blows bubbles from the exhaust pipe. Everyone roars with laughter!
final: Finish! We are first!
All cross the finish together, and {crowd} clap.
All cross the finish together under the chequered flag, and {crowd} clap. {name} and {fr} jump for joy!
A race for friends!
{rival} shakes hands and invites everyone for a ride.
{rival} toots a friendly horn and invites everyone to drive round the track without a race, just for fun.

open: We are {place_in}!
{name} and {fr} run {place_to}.
Today is {event}! {npc} wags a tail, and {crowd} are already crowding at the gate.
Woof! Meow! Hooray!
The zoo is noisy: everyone is getting ready for the party.
The zoo is noisy and merry: the giraffe brushes its teeth, the baby elephant bathes, and {npc} calls everyone to gather.
Morning {place_in}!
The sun rises, and {npc} greets all the animals.
The sun rises, and {npc} goes round to say hello to all the animals. {name}, are you ready for an adventure?
fact: Giraffe's tongue!
A giraffe's tongue is dark and very long: nearly half a metre.
Did you know? A giraffe's tongue is almost half a metre long, and its dark colour, scientists think, protects it from the sun.
A nose like a fingerprint!
Every dog has a nose with its own pattern, like a fingerprint.
Did you know? Every dog's nose has its own pattern, like people's fingerprints. No two are the same!
Eighteen toes!
A cat has just eighteen toes on its paws.
Did you know? A cat has five toes on each front paw and four on each back paw, eighteen in all.
Wombat cubes!
A wombat leaves marks shaped like little cubes.
Did you know? The wombat is the only animal that leaves marks shaped like little cubes, not balls.
fun: Meow-woof!
{rival} barks like a dog, and the dog meows back.
{rival} suddenly barks like a dog, and the dog nearby meows back. All the animals look at each other, unsure who is who.
Elephant and mouse!
A baby elephant saw a mouse and hid behind a bush.
A baby elephant saw a tiny mouse and hid behind a bush, but its trunk stayed out. {crowd} roar with laughter!
Monkeys!
A little monkey grabbed the spyglass and peeks through it.
A little monkey grabbed the spyglass and now watches the zoo as if at the cinema. "How funny you all are!" it says.
The parrot!
The parrot repeats "Woof!", and everyone laughs.
The parrot repeats everything: "Woof! Woof!" And {rival} purrs back without meaning to, and laughs.
final: Hooray, animals! Friends!
{crowd} jump, and {name} strokes everyone.
{crowd} jump and spin, {npc} barks with joy, and {rival} purrs nearby. {name} strokes everyone.
The party is a hit!
{rival} and {npc} dance together, and everyone claps.
{rival} and {npc} dance side by side like best friends, and {crowd} clap their paws and wings.

open: We are {place_in}!
{name} and {fr} hurry {place_to}.
Today is {event}! {npc} clicks claws, and {crowd} are already swirling at the entrance.
Splash! Hooray!
The waves whisper, and {npc} calls everyone into the water.
The waves whisper softly, the sun sparkles on the water, and {npc} clicks claws and calls everyone to dive.
Morning by the sea!
The shore smells of salt, and {npc} lays out shells.
The shore smells of salt and seaweed, and {npc} lays out shells. {name}, are you ready to dive?
fact: Three hearts!
An octopus has three hearts, and its blood is blue.
Did you know? An octopus has three hearts, and its blood is blue because it has a lot of copper.
Otters hold paws!
Sea otters sleep holding paws so they do not drift apart.
Did you know? Sea otters sleep on the water holding each other's paws, so the waves cannot pull them apart.
A crab walks sideways!
A crab walks sideways: it suits its legs best.
Did you know? Crabs walk sideways because their leg joints bend to the side. It is quicker and easier.
A star with no brain!
A starfish has no brain, but crawls to find food.
Did you know? A starfish has no brain, but it still crawls to find food and senses light at the tips of its arms.
fun: A hamster in the water!
{rival} puffs out his cheeks and floats like a buoy.
{rival} fills his cheeks with air and floats on the waves like a buoy. "I am a boat!" he shouts.
Claws!
{npc} wants to hug everyone at once, but catches flippers.
{npc} wants to hug everyone at once, but catches {fr}'s flippers in the claws. They spin in a funny dance.
Blub-blub!
A little fish blows bubbles and sings "la-la-la" underwater.
A little fish blows bubbles and sings underwater. It comes out as "blub-blub-la", and {crowd} roar with laughter.
Little octopus!
An octopus put socks on all eight arms.
An octopus put socks on all eight arms and cannot remember which is the left one. "All right ones!" it decides.
final: Hooray, the sea! Friends!
{crowd} swirl, and {name} and {fr} laugh.
{crowd} swirl in a ring, {npc} clicks claws in time, and {name} and {fr} dance on the sand.
A party by the water!
{rival} gives everyone a shell, and all are happy.
{rival} puffs out his cheeks and gives everyone a shell. Now the shore has the kindest party ever!
